body:
You can't have a democracy without voting -- period, end of story, full stop. Saying that "voting isn't a fundamental right" is basically admitting that your state isn't a real democracy. Kansas told its citizens that with this decision, regardless of the legalese they used.
This isn't just a step backward for Kansas, it's a step backward for our country. Fuel our efforts to fight rulings like this and pass pro-democracy, pro-voter legislation that defends our right to vote with $25 or more right now >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=092224_3&amount=25]
Voter Action Project Logo [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-weekly?refcode=092224_3&amount=25]
Witchita Eagle: Kansas Supreme Court finds Kansans have no ‘fundamental right’ to vote [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=092224_3&amount=25]
Sit down before you read this, Team: The Kansas Supreme Court has ruled that voting is not a fundamental right protected by the Kansas Constitution .
It should go without saying, but this decision will likely weaken legal challenges to future voting restrictions in Kansas and make it easier for opponents of voting rights in their legislature to more aggressively pursue new anti-voting laws.
Hang with us while we explain how they split hairs on this decision, but -- the Kansas Supreme Court said voting is a " political right " and not a " fundamental right ". What's the difference? With a fundamental right, the government has to prove why it needs to pass new voting laws and restrictions. With a political right, the onus is on the voters to prove they are being unreasonably burdened and blocked from voting.
In short -- this decision reads like a " get out of jail free " card from Monopoly, granting a legal wink and a nudge to opponents of voting rights to make it harder to vote.
Voter suppression anywhere hurts us everywhere. Help us defend the right to vote with $25 or whatever you can today in states like Kansas where our democracy is under threat >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=092224_3&amount=25]

Fuel our efforts to fight rulings like this and pass pro-democracy, pro-voter legislation that defends our right to vote with $25 or more right now >> [] Voter Action Project Logo [] Witchita Eagle: Kansas Supreme Court finds Kansans have no ‘fundamental right’ to vote [] Sit down before you read this, Team: The Kansas Supreme Court has ruled that voting is not a fundamental right protected by the Kansas Constitution . It should go without saying, but this decision will likely weaken legal challenges to future voting restrictions in Kansas and make it easier for opponents of voting rights in their legislature to more aggressively pursue new anti-voting laws. Hang with us while we explain how they split hairs on this decision, but -- the Kansas Supreme Court said voting is a " political right " and not a " fundamental right ". What's the difference? With a fundamental right, the government has to prove why it needs to pass new voting laws and restrictions. With a political right, the onus is on the voters to prove they are being unreasonably burdened and blocked from voting. In short -- this decision reads like a " get out of jail free " card from Monopoly, granting a legal wink and a nudge to opponents of voting rights to make it harder to vote. Voter suppression anywhere hurts us everywhere. name: Elissa Slotkin
subject: A little bit about me
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ELISSA SLOTKIN FOR MICHIGAN
body:
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=1963%2E135344%2ECy_FfQ)

Friend --
An open Senate seat in Michigan is a rare opportunity. With the retirement of the great Senator Debbie Stabenow, Republicans will be doing everything they can to win this swing seat and control of the Senate.
**I’m running for Senate because we need a new generation of leaders who think differently, work harder, and _never forget_ that we are public servants.** Being of service to the American people means bringing passionate, pragmatic leadership to Washington.
Service is something I’ve done my entire adult life -- first in the CIA, where I served three tours in Iraq alongside the U.S. military, and later at the White House, State Department, and finally at the Pentagon, as an appointee of President Obama. Thanks to people like you, I’ve served two full terms in Congress, winning three extremely competitive elections in a Republican district.
**[A contribution of $3 or more today will help us show everyone we'll have what it takes to win this election. Please chip in today to help us raise the resources we need to win in this notorious swing state.**](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-sep24.1Cpmdt&refcode=em240922-4-900&amount=3&t=2&akid=1963%2E135344%2ECy_FfQ)
_If you 've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution instantly:_

---

| **[Donate $100](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/123?c0=ebs-em-sep24.t6R_Gf&refcode=em240922-4-900&t=24&akid=1963%2E135344%2ECy_FfQ)**

---
****
But separate from my national security background, what motivated me to first run in 2018 was much more personal – my mom. She was diagnosed with stage IV ovarian cancer in 2009 – and she didn't have health insurance at the time. She had let it lapse after the insurance companies had gouged her for years because she happened to have a pre-existing condition. She passed away in 2011, but that experience – of desperately trying to get her care at the same moment we were filling out bankruptcy paperwork – fueled me to run when the GOP threatened protections for people with pre-existing conditions.
Now Republicans want to put Social Security and Medicare on the same chopping block. Prescription drug costs continue to spiral out of control, and many have to choose between life-saving medicine and their rent or food. We are not settled, as a nation, on access to healthcare and this issue requires real change in Washington. **By winning this Senate seat, we’ll help ensure that Democrats retain the majority and can pass legislation that expands access to healthcare.**
**[Congress desperately needs a new approach to leadership. I would be the youngest Democratic woman in the Senate, if elected. Your contribution of $3 or more today will help us make sure everyone knows what’s at stake in this election.**](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-sep24.1Cpmdt&refcode=em240922-4-900&amount=3&t=27&akid=1963%2E135344%2ECy_FfQ)

Last week, Israel organized a series of attacks across Lebanon that killed dozens and injured thousands, at the very same time that the country's murderous leadership continued its genocidal violence to its South targeting Palestinians in Gaza.
While Israel's disregard for international law has grown outrageously well-established and accepted by figures across Washington, last week's attacks represent a new low in the history of state terrorism. They threaten not only international law, and whatever vestiges of security might remain in the Middle East, but also users of electronic devices around the world--including here in the United States.

### **Expanding conflict in the Middle East**
The most immediate impact of Israel's operation targeting Hezbollah is the risk of inviting an expansion of the violence that has already gripped southern Israel and Gaza. The genocide waged by Netanyahu as the Israeli Defense Forces continue to launch indiscriminate attacks on civilian targets was bad enough before, before Israel turned its sights on Lebanon. Having also recently bombed Syria, Israel finds itself inviting outright war on three distinct fronts.
The extent of this week's violence was gruesome, and particularly reprehensible when considered in context.
Monday's attacks leveraged the previous interception of pager shipments by the Mossad, and killed dozens of figures across Lebanon. While many of them may have been affiliated with Hezbollah, some of them obviously were not, like the 10 year-old girl killed by the Mossad without any regard for civilian casualties or collateral damage.
The initial attacks appeared engineered to maximize casualties among intended targets. Reportedly, the devices buzzed with an alert for a few seconds in order to draw the attention of the intended targets, who suffered various injuries to their faces and hands when handling devices that literally blew up in their faces.
The second round of attacks, however, were engineered to maximize casualties among _random_ targets, like those attending funerals for people killed the day before. The second round of attacks also weaponized an expanding array of electronic devices, including walkie-talkies and even solar panels.
Israel has previously targeted Hezbollah in Lebanon, as well as state actors in both Iran and Syria, with targeted assassinations over the past year, as well as [strikes targeting civilian institutions](https://substack.com/redirect/6139eae6-6bfd-49fb-a18d-edb70a6f97c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) including hospitals and schools. The latest attacks injured more people by orders of magnitude, inviting the escalation that other actors, from Iran to Syria and Lebanon, have to this point managed to avoid.
Having inflicted maximum civilian casualties, Israel has effectively thrown down a gauntlet demanding the expansion of conflict.
### **Tactics over strategy**
On the one hand, the effectiveness of Israel's interception of commercial supply chains and ability to injure thousands of individual targets through an attack seemingly [planned for months](https://substack.com/redirect/78f1968c-a4fc-40ad-9fc3-3caaee3123c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (if not years) is impressive, to say the least.
On the other hand, last week's attacks could offer a case study in how successful tactics can undermine strategy.
In particular, Israel has [galvanized opinion in Lebanon](https://substack.com/redirect/324c9887-5f65-4060-90c8-1b3df6ddec1e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Voices who previously supported de-escalation have turned, in the wake of the attacks, to increasingly favor retaliatory escalation in response to the [fear internalized across the entire country](https://substack.com/redirect/7efc5c0d-48e3-4247-a76e-0fbd51018fba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--not just of an international antagonist, but also the entire spectrum of consumer electronics used on a daily basis by millions of people.
### **Solar panels? Really?**
Among the sets of electronics weaponized by the Mossad last week were solar panels. That should disturb anyone, particularly because it cynically targeted victims based in part on their responses to the climate crisis, creating justifiable fear of technology that we need people to widely adopt.
When I spoke last week on Flashpoints, the host Dennis Bernstein was especially outraged by the weaponization of solar panels. I shared his concern, while noting that the horses already ran out of that proverbial barn.

Years ago, the CIA was criticized for using a [fake immunization campaign in Pakistan](https://substack.com/redirect/127d0b92-062e-45db-8254-2737ebb06221?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as a basis for an intelligence operation. Any public health worker should have been concerned, even long before [the U.S. began bombing doctors](https://substack.com/redirect/b8a8af4d-e8da-4b7d-88f5-b33bf970db21?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) working for international nonprofits.
### **Device security and legitimating future attacks on users**
Some observers have claimed that the consumer electronics devices detonated in Lebanon last week were targeted at Hezbollah, but the reality suggests otherwise. Because Israel intercepted the components it weaponized before the point of manufacture and distribution, they could effectively end up anywhere, especially given the possibility of individuals selling their electronics (for instance, to upgrade to a new model) or allowing friends to borrow them.
That's precisely why international law has long prohibited booby traps. Lama Fakih, Middle East and North Africa director at Human Rights Watch, [explained](https://substack.com/redirect/c688981e-afd0-4c39-93e4-7be018735db8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the international prohibition of bobby traps particularly applies to "objects that civilians are likely to be attracted to or are associated with normal civilian daily use," and that any use of "an explosive device whose exact location could not be reliably known would be unlawfully indiscriminate...."
One reason international law has long prohibited actions like torture--until George W. Bush and Dick Cheney revived it and [Barack Obama decided it was OK](https://substack.com/redirect/e78a093a-1b73-4237-89d5-18f6dc54dcab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--was because all parties recognized the need to stop proliferation, and to guard the rights of their own citizens by respecting the rights of others. Israel's weaponization of consumer electronics opens the door to other countries--including North Korea, Iran, or China--following suit, with potentially devastating consequences.
### **Corruption insulating itself with state violence**
One of the most disturbing aspects--not only of last weeks attacks, but the ongoing genocide in general--is its contrivance to serve the political interests of a corrupt leader. Benjamin Netanyahu was born in Brooklyn, and clings to power in Israel, where [he has long been criticized for corruption](https://substack.com/redirect/b67f15cc-c104-434f-a0e9-8e63602bda3f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), precisely and only because the conflict continues.
Should the conflict resolve itself, Netanyahu will productively lose some of the coalition partners who keep him in office. His political future more or less binds him to the genocide, regardless of the interests of Israel, its citizens, or anyone else.
Of course, the U.S. has been down this road before. On the one hand, our Founders anticipated leaders using conflict to serve their own political interests, and designed the Constitution largely as an elaborate attempt to block that from happening. Yet George W. Bush initiated multiple conflicts in the wake of the 9/11 attacks that revealed themselves as strategic blunders, while riding popular support for the wars to his reelection in 2004.
Netanyahu has more or less killed (at least, if not more than) tens of thousands of people, undermined international law, and rendered an entire set of industries unsafe for the sake of his own personal gain. As the head of a nuclear-armed state, his actions resemble those of some of the most morally reprehensible actors in human history.
### **International law and accountability **
Strategies designed to maximize civilian casualties violate international law and demand accountability. Voices around the world have accordingly decried the new weaponization of consumer electronics, recognizing the threat it poses to civilians in all countries and well-settled principles of international law.
Among them were [a group of United Nations human rights experts](https://substack.com/redirect/d7c39b1a-3ee1-4d8b-90a7-2e9860ec6a67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) who described Israel's actions as constituting "terrifying" violations of international law. They wrote:
> [A]t the time of the attacks there was no way of knowing who possessed each device and who was nearby. Simultaneous attacks by thousands of devices would inevitably violate humanitarian law, by failing to verify each target, and distinguish between protected civilians and those who could potentially be attacked for taking a direct part in hostilities.
According to UCLA law professor [Jessica Peake](https://substack.com/redirect/7fdad4f9-075c-4e03-829b-2ad157f3173b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "detonating pagers in people's pockets without any knowledge of where those are, in that moment, is a pretty evident indiscriminate attack." She described the violation of international law as "quite blatant...violations of both proportionality and indiscriminate attacks."
But don't hold your breath. Israel has pursued an analogous policy for decades, particularly over the last year. It bombed a school in Gaza on the very same day that it detonated pagers across Lebanon, and followed its remote explosions across the country with yet [another random airstrike](https://substack.com/redirect/6139eae6-6bfd-49fb-a18d-edb70a6f97c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Saturday that killed another 37 people, including women and children. It also [raided the West Bank offices of Al-Jazeera](https://substack.com/redirect/9cce675c-e950-433d-9471-d78f7c235823?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), presumably in order to block independent journalism from exposing the Netanyahu regime's continuing--and escalating--violations of international law.
[Global condemnation](https://substack.com/redirect/ff4d9daf-8ce8-46d4-a7d8-d21f8794b858?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has not been enough to restrain Israel, which continues to enjoy carte blanche from Washington. Even as Democrats and Republicans froth at the mouth over the upcoming presidential election, [both of the major parties' candidates](https://substack.com/redirect/4f43cca6-fd0b-4542-a3c9-4d18353de7c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) have endorsed Netanyahu's disregard for laws once held sacrosanct across the globe.

She described the violation of international law as "quite blatant...violations of both proportionality and indiscriminate attacks." But don't hold your breath. Israel has pursued an analogous policy for decades, particularly over the last year. It bombed a school in Gaza on the very same day that it detonated pagers across Lebanon, and followed its remote explosions across the country with yet on Saturday that killed another 37 people, including women and children. It also , presumably in order to block independent journalism from exposing the Netanyahu regime's continuing--and escalating--violations of international law. has not been enough to restrain Israel, which continues to enjoy carte blanche from Washington. Even as Democrats and Republicans froth at the mouth over the upcoming presidential election, have endorsed Netanyahu's disregard for laws once held sacrosanct across the globe. Help inform your friends! Meanwhile, Washington continues to stand as on the world stage. That should be no surprise. Under administrations from each of the corporate political parties, Washington & Langley have widely used drones to bomb essentially random gatherings despite the predictable, , and repeated collateral damage implicit in bomb campaigns. Even the "double tap" strategy evident in Israel's attacks on Tuesday, killing random bystanders who were mourning casualties from the day before--has grown despite global outrage. If voices from around the world clamoring by the millions are not enough to compel Washington's attention, what would be? I envision a future post answering that question, but am eager in the meantime to invite any suggestions in the comments. You're currently a free subscriber to . name: Tammy Baldwin
subject: My least favorite part of this job
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY TAMMY BALDWIN FOR SENATE
body:
[ https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/67?t=1001&akid=3795%2E35263%2EN6GFN5 ]TAMMY BALDWIN FOR SENATE

Sorry to bother you so late on a Sunday,
Peter.

To be honest, asking for donations is my least favorite part of the job.

But the truth is it’s absolutely necessary if we’re going to keep pace
with the flood of Republican spending in this race.

You see, Republicans have already poured $45 million (and counting) toward
ads across Wisconsin. My opponent has self-funded his campaign with $13
million of his own personal fortune to try and drown us out, and there’s
even more on the way.

This is a critical moment,
Peter, because recent polls show
this race is statistically tied, and our final FEC end-of-quarter deadline
before Election Day is just over a week away.

We need to reach our fundraising goals if we’re going to counter the surge
of Republican spending and make sure voters across the state hear our
messages in these crucial final weeks before early voting starts across

body:
[](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/ZkMHapaWy3VxxWvW1giY-Q~~/AAVLBgA~/RgRo0-_UhRkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbVgEAAAAAA~~)

Friend,

The last several months have given us some of the most memorable events in American campaign history -- can you believe it's only been a few months since the fateful Atlanta Presidential Debate between **[President Trump](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/ZkMHapaWy3VxxWvW1giY-Q~~/AAVLBgA~/RgRo0-_UhRkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbVgEAAAAAA~~)** and Joe Biden?

Then came President Trump's survival of a deadly assassination attempt in Pennsylvania and his nomination, along with my conservative GOP Senate colleague from Ohio, running mate **[J.D. Vance,](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/ZkMHapaWy3VxxWvW1giY-Q~~/AAVLBgA~/RgRo0-_UhRkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbVgEAAAAAA~~)** Joe Biden's withdrawal from the race, the Democrats' coronation of radical Kamala Harris and her selection of leftist Minnesota Governor Tim Walz.

But with all of this change, _one thing hasn 't:_ I'm counting on you, no matter what happens in these final, pivotal weeks of the campaign, **[to stand with me and win this decisive Nebraska U.S. Senate race.](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/ZkMHapaWy3VxxWvW1giY-Q~~/AAVLBgA~/RgRo0-_UhRkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbVgEAAAAAA~~)**

The disastrous leftist agenda of the **[Biden-Harris Democrats](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/ZkMHapaWy3VxxWvW1giY-Q~~/AAVLBgA~/RgRo0-_UhRkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbVgEAAAAAA~~)** must be stopped -- and reversed. That opportunity is rapidly approaching with the 2024 Elections, friend, **[and that's why I'm contacting you today.](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/ZkMHapaWy3VxxWvW1giY-Q~~/AAVLBgA~/RgRo0-_UhRkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbVgEAAAAAA~~)**

Just like they counted on Kamala Harris' vote as President of the Senate to break dozens of ties in their favor, the Democrats are desperate to keep their control over the Majority to continue their dangerous agenda and avoid accountability for their failures and abuse of power.

To end their schemes -- and begin repairing the damage they've inflicted with commonsense conservative solutions -- we need strong Republican Senators who will follow through with the experience and capability necessary to get things done on Capitol Hill.

We must stay focused on a successful outcome by ensuring we're as prepared as we can be, **[and that starts with supporters like you.](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/ZkMHapaWy3VxxWvW1giY-Q~~/AAVLBgA~/RgRo0-_UhRkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbVgEAAAAAA~~)**

That's why I hope I can count on you **[to step up and make a generous contribution to my 2024 Nebraska U.S. Senate re-election effort immediately!](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/ZkMHapaWy3VxxWvW1giY-Q~~/AAVLBgA~/RgRo0-_UhRkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbVgEAAAAAA~~)**

_Thank you,_ friend.

Best,

**_He could have quit when his family home was raided with deadly force._**
**_He could have quit when partisan left-wing operatives dragged him through a show trial._**
**_And nobody would have blamed him if he quit after facing two close brushes with death._**

Donald J. Trump nearly lost his life for the second time in as many months. President Trump is my running mate, and my friend, but he is more importantly a father and grandfather to people who truly love him. I want him to have many more years with his family. But even when faced with losing everything he holds dear, DONALD J. TRUMP REFUSED TO SURRENDER. He could have quit when his family home was raided with deadly force. He could have quit when partisan left-wing operatives dragged him through a show trial. And nobody would have blamed him if he quit after facing two close brushes with death. But the thought never crossed his mind. He didn’t need politics, but the country needed him. He had everything anyone could ever want in a life. And yet, instead of choosing the easy path, he chose to endure abuse, slander and persecution, all because he loves this country. For the last eight years, President Trump has given everything he has to fight for the people of our country. And for the next 7 weeks of this campaign, President Trump will continue fighting for YOU - no matter the cost. Because he knows the sacrifices will be worth it when we save this country. ---
# Titus Desperately Lies to Stay In Power
---
Dear Peter,
You have a clear choice in Nevada's First Congressional District race. You can choose an honorable and honest military veteran who offers practical solutions to our problems or a career politician who lies to the people she represents. Dina Titus is spending millions of dollars on expensive TV ads. You might think she would use these ads to discuss the issues affecting Nevada families, such as inflation, open borders, failing schools, or Social Security. Or maybe she will talk about her dismal record as a 35-year career politician. Instead, Titus has spent the millions she's received from lobbyists and special interests to lie to her constituents. That's right! Instead of addressing ongoing issues plaguing Nevada, Titus lies about the one issue already settled in Nevada. She is lying about my position on the issue of abortion. My position has not changed. Here it is: Abortion is a settled law in Nevada. A referendum of the people passed it, which means neither the Governor nor the State legislature can overturn it. Only the people of Nevada can change it.
Like 71% of Americans, the people of Nevada think there should be limits on abortion. In Nevada, those limits are 24 weeks, followed by the life and health of the mother. Dina Titus ignored the will of the people when she voted for a federal law to allow abortion up until the day of delivery and to have the government pay for these unlimited abortions.
I support the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe vs Wade, not just because I'm pro-life, but because it is the correct legal decision. Even Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg stated that the Roe decision was on shaky legal ground. There is nothing in the Constitution about abortion.
When the Constitution is silent on a topic, the power is vested in the States and in "We, the people." The people of Nevada have spoken. As your representative in Congress, I will not support any federal action that goes against the will of the people of my district. subject: How should we elect the president?
body:

Dr. Arnn asked us to reach out to you. Do you have five minutes

http://paracom.paramountcommunication.com/p/oWJIYnWWNB

Please see a special message from our
sponsor:

Dear
Fellow American,

Dr. Arnn
asked us to reach out to you. Do you have five minutes to take
our survey on the Electoral College? We would greatly value your
input.

If so,
here is a link to the survey:
http://paracom.paramountcommunication.com/ct/63575563:WJIYnWWNB:m:3:2627245898:2B1FCF2E784A474AF99CED6F9DAF63F7:r

Sincerely,

Hillsdale
College

---------- Forwarded message ---------
From:
Larry P. Arnn
Subject:
Survey on an urgent matter

Friend,

I am
enclosing a survey on a very urgent matter.

It will
only take a moment of your time, but the topic is vital to our
nation's future.

A
movement is growing, led by progressives-but supported by many
well-meaning Americans-to change the way we elect our president.
In effect, it seeks to do away with the Electoral College as
devised by the Framers of our Constitution.

That's
why Hillsdale College is conducting a National Survey on
Presidential Selection.

By
completing this survey and returning it to me as soon as
possible, you will help Hillsdale College more clearly understand
the views of mainstream Americans concerning this issue-views we
will make available to policymakers and opinion leaders.

You can
complete the National Survey on Presidential Selection by using
the link below:
http://paracom.paramountcommunication.com/ct/63575563:WJIYnWWNB:m:3:2627245898:2B1FCF2E784A474AF99CED6F9DAF63F7:r

For most
of our nation's history, the Electoral College, as devised by the
Framers of our Constitution, was not controversial. Indeed, it
was considered essential to preserving free and representative
government.

But
today, more than a dozen states have joined together in an
attempt to undermine this constitutional bulwark of liberty.

This
movement to undermine the Constitution has grown largely because
of the failure of America's schools to provide young people with
a proper grounding in American civics-too many Americans simply
don't understand the importance of the Constitution, including
the Electoral College, to liberty.

Because
of this, Hillsdale College has expanded its educational mission
on behalf of liberty nationwide, directly teaching millions of
Americans in all 50 states.

These
efforts, which aim to counter the Left's domination over most of
our schools, include:

Teaching millions of citizens nationwide through free online
courses, such as ";Constitution 101" and ";The Great American
Story: A Land of Hope;"

Reaching over six million households and businesses nationwide
with Imprimis, Hillsdale's free digest of liberty;

Promoting constitutional education through social media outlets
popular with young people;

Sending millions of pocket-size copies of America's founding
documents to citizens and K-12 schools across America; and

Restoring excellence to K-12 education by helping establish and
guiding classical K-12 schools nationwide and providing, free of
charge, Hillsdale's American classical K-12 curriculum (including
American civics) to thousands of American educators and
homeschoolers.

Your
answers to the National Survey on Presidential Selection will
help Hillsdale form the most effective strategy to educate
millions of Americans about the importance of the Constitution to
liberty-including the importance of the Electoral College.

And this
is especially important in this critical time for America's
future.

So please
share your views on this urgent topic by completing our National
Survey on Presidential Selection and returning it to me as soon
as possible. It will only take a few minutes of your time.

You can
take the survey using this secure link I've provided below:
http://paracom.paramountcommunication.com/ct/63575563:WJIYnWWNB:m:3:2627245898:2B1FCF2E784A474AF99CED6F9DAF63F7:r

And after
you take your survey, I hope you will also consider supporting
Hillsdale College with a tax-deductible gift.

Since
1844, Hillsdale has been ";pursuing truth and defending liberty."
Today, it does so through its extensive educational outreach
efforts while refusing to accept ONE PENNY of government
funding-not even indirectly in the form of federal or state
student grants or loans.

The
support of private citizens like you is essential to our work.

Please
represent your state and take the National Survey on Presidential
Selection today. Thank you for your time and attention-and for
your friendship and support of liberty.

Warm
regards,

Larry P.
Arnn

President, Hillsdale College
Pursuing
Truth and Defending Liberty Since 1844

## Harris, Trump Eye "60 Minutes" Interviews
Former President Donald Trump and Vice President Kamala Harris are [considering doing interviews](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxsj7FurDAQRb_G7oyGscG7hYvX0O1rUyIvHi8TGYyMF5K_j0id7kpXOkfn4zE-PCdeX__9Qq7GPPqp8kHjXaFWaEYjg4tESFqSay3aFkDbm5zdBKabiFr0E_ba6hat7rUhMDbeYveU7BDQwB11C2C7rkEbuhAhWjI38uEpDFDgmkvzmXmtM8X0nQ8qzZQXmdxc67YL_U_gIHA4z7PxX5z36xU4XGyBA9yvjQKH2ZfCu6rlvWyqB7Xw-q60K14rlYPplMWF7eSUeO-tMPBaPKdfV_27_HD4EwAA__95qlnD) on the CBS news program _60 Minutes_ that would air back-to-back on Oct. 7 as a campaign grand finale.Neither Harris nor Trump has accepted the invitation yet, but both [reportedly have it under consideration.](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxskLtuxCAQAL_G7jjBGrNQUKS57tKmtLBZzhvhhzBnK38fXeqUo2lG8_UYHoEzr8_PsJCvaRvCVPmkwQnoBOhBt9EnIqCuJa8QUEnZoW1n7zRYNBMka7QLijBpohQ1jLFXGKllDxK0dNApKbHvb4Cxj0kmJG0pxLHRkiLXrdy-N17rTCn_bCeV27QtbfZzrfvRdB8N3Bu4h32l63irN5TKU6YG7rW8ll3MoRQ-hJFi4fVV6RC8Vion0yWskmMwABiQSMFkyFpCGZ2z_egctsXH_eKc-TDYaPlcAue_hPr_kNPDbwAAAP___GRiBA)The quadrennial CBS special typically airs separate interviews with the candidates back-to-back, giving voters one of their last chances before the election to evaluate the two in tandem.The Trump campaign has said the former president won't participate in another debate, despite [Harris' acceptance of a CNN invite](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxskLFurDAQRb_GdEZmbDAULl5Dt69NiYw9LBMZG5nJovx9tKnTXelKR0fn47E8PCXKz__-QMdbWXxgeuEySdASzGKa6DZEQN2g6yzYTiltx2Z3YdX9NOlVdwFMB6OPo1_jMKDyA0AcGnKgwKgJdKeU7fsWbOzjpjaLZkQfV2EURuJS289CmXfc0nd5YW1DOZrkdubzEvqfgFnAfN93G_Ia3qeA-Y0WMKvpvTsB8-5rpUv6Z0W8JBd5FsbM5JMMOcuIq2eUN_EuuX4dpyxZlsASdLvzkZrq4nlTSnQNVhj1PDylXxH-O8vLwU8AAAD__63gZEs) for a second debate on Oct. 23.
## Judge's Murder Rocks Kentucky Town
A small Kentucky town is reeling after its sheriff was charged [in the shooting death](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxskLGu4yAQAL_G7oiWZW2goLgmXa690iKw2CTERDZOlL8_5dWvHE0zmn-X6eJzyev81z_YtVQnH1p-8WQFKoE0UR9dYkZWPTupUUsApU2_OEkGJIWIZEYFZrxKaTkxjONVIhD02SEggUUlAfQwnFDHISZImsmwj9eOgGNudTvdal7bwql86ou3U6iPvriltefeqT8dnjs8--fK7_2rvrC1HAp3eL7z2o5w_4h94S2nJG5HnFmEemxtqcfOYl9qbXmdRTQxDTaRJEBFxg6o2XpOZBMFE1K_ufh851LyPuqOYH74XH5a2u9nXg7_BwAA___mJGU5) of the county's only judge in his courthouse chambers.The preliminary investigation suggests that Letcher County Sheriff Shawn "Mickey" Stines shot and killed Judge Kevin Mullins after an argument in the courthouse, but [no motive has been named thus far.](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxskLGO4yAURb8Gd0TwsENcUGxDN9tuGWF4xC_BMAs4Vv5-5a2nu8WVztH583X_cpQoP367DU2P5e58pzfeZw6Kw3gfh2AiIqAa0EgNWgqh9G1YTRidVLflOstlkurmlzEqvyB4tyxilteBDAgYxQxKCqGn6QI6TCGKqHG8oQsLGwUG6qVenoVyXzGmT3ljvfiyDcmsvX83pn4xsAzscRwXX_ZKWPmz7DW7dP4Y2NZL_TCwGY_GwPpKGzKwJ5yBFfO5JQP7wtx3__rw5x4eyF_4psy3PSXKjbe1lE75wduKlWLkG_kXfnjrlLHxrZxV-N8dW6eST46elJyuQguhGdihmvB9UErUrpqN4rE5-i849J-zvg38CwAA__8WaXss)The two men were reportedly old friends and had lunch together just before the shooting.Sheriff Stines was recently deposed in a federal investigation into a former deputy who had pleaded guilty to raping a woman in Judge Mullins' chambers. It's not known whether this played into the argument that led to the shooting. [Stines surrendered to authorities](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxs0DGO6yAUheHV2B0WXBNjCorXuMtrp7QwXAwJgQhwrOx-lNGU033SaY7-r-t61SGGtP_XD1TN5VWbFl64SgIjAb7y3iqHCDj2qJgAwSgdxdx7ZeU00o0aMUmuxSaZhonNM-MG5Cap7oMCCpxKGBml4nIZQNiLddQJ5DNqu3Wcog0tl-GWQ2oeXXznF5bB5EcflW_tWbvxXwdLB8t5nkPaTMKzfvYOlg87WI5KftWK3tG-yR1TO8z9TarHEpwjxuuyoyVONx2JyUdpPh8VSfU5t5B2cjvsjqS2I1VSTNJMMDmNfVH2eYYYQ51Ex-n-0CH-vGt_t3op-A4AAP__rclung) at the courthouse following the shooting.
## Sunken Yacht May Hold Classified Data
The $40 million superyacht that capsized off Italy in August, killing billionaire Mike Lynch and six others, may contain [top-secret documents and confidential data](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxskL2O5CAQBp8GZz2C9g92QHCJs7n0QgtDM-aEDcItj7xPv5qNN_ukTyqV6t9zedqY4vH6a3cyHPJiHceLlgmwBeyWrvEmECG1DRmlUSspWz02m1mHsddTcGoKdnRuXIOjXqmBqB3V0A5NNCixkxO2Skrd9w_UvvdBBk3dSNavopPkI-f6-J_jwRuFdOeL6sPlvUlmYy6naP8InAXOx13yyZ9L4PwBC5zl9NlK4PzONXk46H0KnLnmiyAH4FzgJFeJIR4hw25vWAm42lLIQz5gtTed0R5wW7cx2MBUwZP16QZnyxm_CCqVXFng3FTjyzumFM9Bi06-dhvTjyz_nu4y-B0AAP__jmtyRA) on foreign governments in water-tight safes.Italian prosecutors have ordered heightened security around the wreck, believing it holds encrypted hard drives with classified data tied to Western intelligence services.Lynch, a former adviser to British prime ministers and recently acquitted in a U.S. fraud case, had strong ties to Western intelligence through his companies, [notably Darktrace,](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxskD_vpCAUAD8Ndhh8oGhBcY3dXnul4c9zfbcIRtg1fvvLXv2rJ5lM5s9jeViKlJ6_7Y6mrnmxvtIHl4mD5KAW1QSzIgLKBk2nQXdCSD02m9FWuUF2IijXj36SqNzYe-V6K72VtmvIgAAlJpCdELrvW9ChD6tYNaoRbXBMCQxU89n-zZTqhmu88wfP1ue9iWar9ShM_mIwM5iv62opBTwwBUy19bl9vxjMCa_yxfmMgcGM7zMfyGB29sZCNvHyPvC8rd8qL5RelJ58pxfyeCe_8Xr7nBOPtmKp_CvjDoZuGPqp3eoem9OE46IYqQyaKfHcLcX_gfXnXR8D_wIAAP__gPxvyQ) an AI-driven cybersecurity firm. Stephen Chamberlain, Lynch's business partner and co-defendant in the U.S. fraud case, died after he was hit by a car [just one day after the yacht incident](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxsj71utDAQAJ_G7g6t139c4eJr6O5rUyJjr--MDEZgQZKnjy51upFGGmk-HuPD55LX53-_kGupjj60fNJ4v6G8oRoVjy4RIUlOTli0AkDanr9cDFpq0D2iMoaSCX4yRotobVQkouLZIaCCO0oBYLXu0EYdEyRLqicfJ6aAYm517-aa1_aiVL7qSXsX6sKLe7W2HUz-YzgwHK7r6qYpvB3DYaXrYDj4veVQ6I0B5q2I77kXn5XvLm5XLiUfxjIFz8Xn8lttfz-eDn8CAAD__45rU2U).

Friend -- We will be making a very important announcement tonight about an upcoming event to be held in Manhattan. While we are all greatly relieved that President Biden (or whoever tells him what to do) listened to the Department of Defense, as opposed to the State Department, and told Britih Prime Minister Keir Starmer that Ukraine will not be allowed to use American-made-and-guided long range missiles to strike targets within Russian territory, which would have provoked a Russian military response, the threat is not over. As former USMC Intelligence Officer and UN Weapons Inspector Scott Ritter put it, "On Saturday we were 72 minutes away from Armageddon." There is no guarantee that the war mongers' cabal are going to give up on their fool's errand of "forcing Russia to back down" before the election. There have already been two assassination attempts against former President Donald Trump, the latest by a Ukrainian Azov-affiliated dupe, because fears are running high that a Trump Presidency would bring the Ukraine-Russia proxy war to a negotiated end. There are important peace rallies this weekend in Kingston, NY and in Washington, D.C. Jose and I will have a strong presence in both places, and we want you to join us. We must strengthen the mobilization for peace, both in Ukraine, and also in Southwest Asia, where our guest of last week, Dr. Mark Perlmutter reported on his observations from a medical tour in Gaza, and his estimate that over 92,000 Palestinians have been killed. Israel is expanding that war, with terror explosions of pagers and other devices supposedly being used by Hezbollah members, which killed at least 40 people, including innocent children, followed by a massive bombing spree in southern Lebanon. If someone from a distant galaxy were to look at what mankind is doing on earth, they would probably be unable to explain why such a talented species was trying so hard to annihilate itself! We must change course before it's too late. | [](https://www.sareforsenate.com/sare_vega_and_friends_20240923?e=bd1d687cdeff164927fc1e159dca3e71&utm_source=sareforsenate&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=20240922_zoom&n=2 "RSVP for Zoom Link for Mon. 8:30 pm") [RSVP for Zoom Link for Mon. 8:30 pm](https://www.sareforsenate.com/sare_vega_and_friends_20240923?e=bd1d687cdeff164927fc1e159dca3e71&utm_source=sareforsenate&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=20240922_zoom&n=2)

## Enchanted Rock State Park Expanding
The Texas Parks and Wildlife Department has [approved the purchase](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kLGOnDAQQL8GulmZweB14SLNdpc2JRrbA1jx4pM9LLd_H-X669-Tnt6fj-WDUk7H9pue7ORrLQsFSS9eLOAIqBfdR-dVtEPPbjBolB3vE_a7m_FurF29N_cYKcxszOCjDcYrmkzQfXKoUCuL46CmeRxu2sz3MCJ67X1AXDutOCYp9SY7C39RW_O7vLjeQnn22e0in60bf3X46PBxXdetUThr5UP-Ex0-Dr5ah49vF_aUM4RyHlLfDfgIOx3CEWoJf6EJCcNBclbKQJUJUgPy5RSQAhsLXPQGn7aNK4zTPEwWsa8ufl4p59Rm02m1PSnl7zr5YdbL4b8AAAD___i2bwo) of 630 acres to expand the Enchanted Rock Natural Area in Gillespie and Llano counties. The park's main attraction is the dome-shaped [425-foot-tall pink granite rock](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kLHOpCAURp8Gu2vwiqgFxTQmW8y2WxrQq5IgzAIj49tvZvu__PIlJyfnz3N-auus33_rk1T-bGHWS7YXzSNgCyhmUa3K8HVsKlJNjz0f26HD6lBSSjG2A2-kHDYynLqhH1bCZeOrMbyrrEKOgo_YNryTbVOLXg5Li2iEMQvixgSn1eYQ63xQpo9Om7vDRbFewlk5deT8Sqx9MJwYTqWU-kz--zGcyMM7MZxy1Bc5hpOn8t3luEHDYZ2DJbx9jjd4nd-R4BUpUbwIbII9hmL9DuaGM0SCfGgPknPQS6QvRkd4PJq_v1YMVVTrq1jnbJI9E3w_tXX_DfMPwS6F_wIAAP__UnFumQ), the largest such rock in the United States. The park boasts 11 miles of hiking trails over 1,644 acres and draws around 250,000 visitors a year, making it one of the most popular state parks in Texas. ## Fort Cavazos Gets New Museum
Fort Cavazos has opened the long-awaited [National Mounted Warrior Museum](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kLuO5CAURL8GZ1hwof0ICDZx1ptuaPGyjRZDC1-b7vn6kSeftEqqOjr_nvNThxjS-lfvXuF7ybO2GC4_jxQEBTnLxinD3Mgbr3gPPRvF8IBmU_JhhOW94dwMwi6yd90wmKUzo_MG_NIEBQwkG0Fw9ugEb2XfDVYAGGmMBViIZN4FzKXFzaN_62OJn3z50tq8N1FtiK-DiD8EJgJTrbX9X_F9lwSme5vAxEYCEx8ITEsuSK2-9Fc-6JajoyUYkxO1J2JIK7W--D2nD405rVRXHdA7mjSGnHSkez7THVRdSsiF7ufhz_upKcq9aogxHF1PJFt3HeIPIv5i7FLwHQAA__8jY3At), a project 13 years in the making that aims to showcase the history and evolution of mounted warfare, from mounted cavalry to modern tanks. I lost three fingers on my left hand in a meat-grinding accident when I was a kid. I am and always will be a farmer, like my folks and like my grandparents. In fact, I’m very proud to be the U.S. Senate’s only working dirt farmer. Every spring, I spend a lot of weeks working the stubble, getting equipment ready for planting, and out in the field seeding. Come summer, I am out there harvesting. I maintain my own heavy equipment and deliver my grain in a truck that’s a bit bigger than what any of my colleagues drive. I buy grease by the case and seeds by the ton. I butcher my own beef. My wife, Sharla, and I work the farm hand-in-hand. The task of scheduling my work in the Senate around the inflexible timing of farm responsibilities drives my staff crazy—but they know my farm work is non-negotiable. It keeps me, quite literally, grounded. And rather than spend my days hobnobbing with special interests, I rely on hard-working folks like you to power everything we do. [That’s why I’m personally asking you to join my reelection team and split $15 between Blue Amp Action and my campaign today to help us defend Montana’s Senate seat. Anything you can give makes a difference.](https://default.salsalabs.org/T3d159041-9d07-4087-8127-513169ae4122/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

| "It needs to build not from the top down but from the bottom up, like supporting solid Republican candidates who can win seats in the heavily Democratic controlled state Legislature. Currently there are only four Republicans in the 40-member Massachusetts State Senate.
One such candidate is Republican Kelly Dooner, a Taunton City Councilor, who is running for the open southeastern Massachusetts Senate seat held by longtime Democrat Sen. Marc Pacheco who did not seek re-election.
It is the first time in 32 years that the seat has been open.
And like campaigns for office elsewhere, including the presidency, illegal immigration is a major issue.
Dooner has raised it in the takeover of the Clarion Hotel in Taunton by the Healey administration to house illegal immigrants without even notifying municipal officials.
'Our state is being bankrupted by the influx of immigrants. We are spending billions, not millions, of dollars to house people who are not legally here in our nation. It is unsustainable and it is unfair to the hard-working taxpayers of the Commonwealth,' she said.
Unlike the Biden administration, which failed to close the border it opened, and Congress, which has also failed to secure it, Dooner at least believes the state can do something to deal with the problem."

Hello,
The system is rigged. We all know it. The only people who can afford to run for Senate full-time are millionaires like my opponent, Republican Deb Fischer.
That’s why they’re the only people who ever win. It’s why the Senate is just another country club full of Ivy League graduates, former business execs, and trust fund babies.
Working people like me, we can’t afford to give up our jobs to run for office. During this campaign, I’ve been working 40, 60, sometimes 90 hours a week as a steamfitter just to pay our bills and put food on the table. How’s anybody with a real job supposed to campaign and win when your opponent is wealthy enough to not work at all?
**That’s why I announced that I am taking a leave from my job as a steamfitter to campaign full-time for the U.S. Senate and keep up our momentum.**
And yes, that means I’m going to need to take a salary from our campaign. Not a big one. Just enough to replace the $48,000 I got paid last year and the cost of health care for me and my family.
Politics shouldn’t only be for the rich, and this is the only way we can change that.
**SIX polls now show me neck-and-neck with my opponent, Republican Deb Fischer – and in one, I am LEADING her by 2 points.** With support from grassroots donors like you, we even out-raised her during the last quarter! But she still has $2.3 million more than us because of her corporate PAC friends.
Together, we are charting the path for how a blue collar, union worker can run for U.S. Senate – and win. **But I need grassroots donors like you to chip in to my campaign right now if we’re going to defeat Republican Deb Fischer and flip this Senate seat:**

Can I tell you a story about my family farm, friend?
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/93371817/500276436/1743277108?&amounts=250,100,50,25,5&refcode=jtk4837-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNzE1MzgxMy1hNDc5LWVmMTEtOTkxYS02MDQ1YmRlZTY2ODEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=i27urFUmvUoR5T0LmbQp2TYcMJRDSAKbxEF-NP2U-3s=)
In 1910, my grandfather came to Montana. He found a piece of grassy land, took a look at it, and said, “This is the place.” And that’s where the farm began.
He farmed the land until the early 1940s and then passed it down to my folks. In 1978, my wife Sharla and I took over the farm, and we’re still here today, three generations and more than 40 years later.
We’ve made a lot of progress here – Sharla and I built a new home, several steel buildings, and more storage.
The truth is, I love this work. Yes, it makes for early mornings and late nights during planting and harvest seasons – but it also keeps me grounded, and it gives me perspective on the issues we face every day.
When I think about climate change, I’m thinking of folks on farms like mine, struggling with catastrophic droughts or historic levels of flooding. When I think about reforming the USPS, I’m thinking of the people in rural communities across Montana who rely on timely mail delivery for their medication or Social Security checks. And when I think about infrastructure, I’m thinking of the rural towns near mine that need access to affordable, high-speed internet.
**These aren’t abstract issues or talking points. They’re very real challenges that deserve real solutions, and that’s what I’m fighting for in Washington. I spend every single day trying to do right by working families, farmers, students, and veterans here in Montana and across the country.**
**[I’m running for reelection because there’s still work to be done. Just like my parents and grandparents on the family farm, when I commit to something, I see it through. Can you make a split donation of any amount today between my campaign and Jacky Rosen’s to help me keep up the fight in Washington?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/93371818/500276437/1743277108?&amounts=250,100,50,25,5&refcode=jtk4837-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNzE1MzgxMy1hNDc5LWVmMTEtOTkxYS02MDQ1YmRlZTY2ODEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=i27urFUmvUoR5T0LmbQp2TYcMJRDSAKbxEF-NP2U-3s=)**

Derek, we’ve got good news and bad news. **We’ll start with the good:** During the presidential debate earlier this month, we saw a surge of individual donations. It was incredible. That’s money that we’re putting to work immediately reaching as many voters as possible, especially now that early voting has started. **But here’s the bad news:** Since the debate, we’ve seen a significant slowdown in donations. The timing couldn’t be worse. Especially because our most important FEC deadline yet is coming up in a matter of days, and in some states, voters are already casting ballots. You can see the dropoff in the last few days. **That means we have two choices to catch up.** We’ll either need _a lot_ more individual donations, or we’ll need Democrats who understand the importance of this moment to give a little bit more when they chip in. Derek, normally we ask people making their first donation of the cycle to give $3 or $7. But today, we are asking you to pitch in a little bit more at this critical time -- $15 if you can. name: Ben Samuels
subject: Online gambling is dangerous. Missourians should vote against it.
body:
In November, Missourians will vote on Amendment 2, a bill that would legalize online sports gambling. You should vote No. Here's why.

| |
---|---|---
| | | Forwarded this email? [Subscribe here](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9iZW5zYW11ZWxzLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.Ji0y5yxAPl277Dj2N_bGYJ_PYBkepcQeNYiQqjASXJ4?) for more
---
# [Online gambling is dangerous. Missourians should vote against it.](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=147244890&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTQ3MjQ0ODkwLCJpYXQiOjE3MjcwOTU3NjQsImV4cCI6MTcyOTY4Nzc2NCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.ut3CNoQNoRJvqiPENpEmCNsYn-E5cMgfM9oMFT4lCvw)
### Missouri's Amendment 2 would legalize online and mobile sports gambling, which is far more harmful than people realize. You should vote No.
| | [Ben Samuels](https://substack.com/@bensamuels)
---
| Sep 23
---
| [](https://substack.com/@bensamuels)
---
---
| | | [](https://substack..W0SYWT5AdL_TQM6w4MJ9OvIqXiNtlqCSM-RWLZqtEY0?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/bensamuels/p/vote-against-amendment-2-in-missouri?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store)
---
Among Missouri's ballot measures, most of the attention has been focused on [Amendment 3](https://substack.com/redirect/31b677de-26a4-42ac-a1cf-b2484e2899db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which would overturn the state's abortion ban. [I've written about that too](https://substack.com/redirect/ac5cd5a1-5929-4fd2-a903-a4350263a38e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg); it's hugely important.
But there's another amendment that we need to focus on: [Amendment 2](https://substack.com/redirect/adfebcf5-e2d5-4fa4-97e8-12ccd81abe22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which would legalize online and mobile sports gambling in Missouri.
In large part because of efforts and lobbying from FanDuel and DraftKings, there are 30 states in the country that have [legalized mobile sports gambling](https://substack.com/redirect/ca8400e5-8452-4b05-bb68-0cfaa4908130?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) since a [Supreme Court ruling in 2018 gave states the right to do so](https://substack.com/redirect/8c043a63-51ee-4b0a-af4b-617fbcb101d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Across those states, what we're [seeing is consistently frightening](https://substack.com/redirect/6e2b0263-4640-4e3c-8035-31dab55f1a1e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
* Gambling addiction is up.
* Debt is up, credit scores are down, and bankruptcy is up. This is especially true among men and among younger people.
* Legalized mobile sports gambling [hasn't generated nearly the tax revenue that its advocates promised it would](https://substack.com/redirect/c8ea9814-f74e-4294-9d36-9b127e115c50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* Making it easier to gamble--which we'd be doing, by essentially giving everyone a casino on their phones--leads to higher rates of domestic violence and higher rates of suicide.

The goal of more funding for education is worthy, but it isn't worth the costs. We have much better ways to fund education.
**Vote No on Amendment 2.** Much more detail below on why this is so important.
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9iZW5zYW11ZWxzLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9hY2NvdW50IiwicCI6MTQ3MjQ0ODkwLCJzIjoyNDQwMzk4LCJmIjp0cnVlLCJ1Ijo5MDUwMTE5MiwiaWF0IjoxNzI3MDk1NzY0LCJleHAiOjE3Mjk2ODc3NjQsImlzcyI6InB1Yi0wIiwic3ViIjoibGluay1yZWRpcmVjdCJ9.n5MynzQWVdJkTn5W0bSJl7T67dk8oAhm1Toezgoa6ck?)
_Please forward this article to any Missouri voters who might not know about Amendment 2, or who might be on the fence._
### Gambling is not inherently bad
I have no problem with gambling; in fact, I actually gamble pretty often. In college, I [wrote an article](https://substack.com/redirect/cbda4f33-ecdf-4d10-a52e-0f0a653070be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)1 about how I grew up gambling. I play in a few regular poker games. I'm in two fantasy football leagues. I've been to Las Vegas just about every year since I turned 21.2
I'm mentioning this to establish that I'm not a gambling abstentionist, nor do I think it should be banned outright. There is some good that comes from gambling, beyond just the fact that (in moderation) it can be fun.
Casinos [employ 750,000 people](https://substack.com/redirect/071ef4f3-0187-4e7c-b4f8-86dfcb05c5db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)3 across the country and [drive tourism](https://substack.com/redirect/2a4176a8-283b-4a94-b51e-b5b9cdf3ed17?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The history of tribal gaming is complex, and [its benefits are wildly uneven in their distribution](https://substack.com/redirect/5db350de-8c24-4b68-bf08-2d693ab38ea2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) among the nation's [574 federally recognized tribes](https://substack.com/redirect/a006b7fa-c5c5-4e5c-9159-98d6803cbb68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), but Indian gaming has [generated huge revenues, employment, and population growth](https://substack.com/redirect/ed0947ce-0ed4-4f7b-98be-318500f3aa85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in and around Indian country.4
For Missourians, [Amendment 2](https://substack.com/redirect/adfebcf5-e2d5-4fa4-97e8-12ccd81abe22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) would basically change two things:
1. It would legalize sports gambling.
2. It would legalize mobile and online gambling.

For lots of reasons I will get into, **mobile gambling would be dangerous for Missourians**. But even beyond that, it's also highly extractive.
Unlike traditional casinos, which [in Missouri employ more than 6,000 people](https://substack.com/redirect/d640049f-af71-4597-b185-a8d40fbdf46c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), mobile sports gambling platforms--namely FanDuel and DraftKings--create no local jobs. They invest in no local infrastructure. FanDuel is based in New York City and DraftKings is based in Boston; beyond a pretty modest tax, there's no reason to think that any of the profits will stay in the state either.
There's a reason that [FanDuel and DraftKings are spending well over $10 million](https://substack.com/redirect/08bbf021-8dd7-4680-abdf-f8ee084fd865?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--so far--to get this amendment passed.
The "Yes" campaign has talked about millions being invested in local education, but even that is suspect.5 In states across the country, legalized mobile gambling [isn't generating the tax revenues that were promised](https://substack.com/redirect/c696a983-0013-4b3b-b9cd-d629b4fef47b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
And beyond that, it's creating all kinds of other issues.
### If sports gambling isn't legal, won't people do it anyway?
Of course. A [United Nations report](https://substack.com/redirect/c2d3f363-b159-487d-8556-9c0e87b2a4e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) claims that $1.7 trillion (!) is gambled illegally on sports every year across the world. In the United States alone, [it's around $60 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/360fc201-b0f3-4296-a169-edf7d1a7467e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
So yes: gambling on sports is happening regardless of whether or not we want it to. That's a very real problem.
But making gambling easier for people--that is to say, creating legal avenues for people to gamble--_does_ make people more likely to gamble. People very demonstrably gamble more and are more likely to engage in other dangerous behaviors when they are near casinos:
* "A casino within 10 miles of home has a significant effect on problem gambling and is associated with a 90 percent increase in the odds of being a pathological or problem gambler." ([Source](https://substack.com/redirect/63918a53-e697-4d8c-a9ac-dbbcec641247?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* "If a respondent had no casinos within 30 miles, he or she had a 2.7% chance of being a problem gambler; if one casino, a 3.9% chance; if six or more, a 6.2% chance. The authors estimate that at least part of this effect is causal." ([Source](https://substack.com/redirect/d746d504-ceee-4987-83b9-ff58e829c1e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* "The negative changes [of nearby Indian casinos] include about a 10 percent increase in auto thefts, larceny, violent crime, and bankruptcy in counties four years after a casino has opened, and an increase in bankruptcies within 50 miles of a new casino." ([Source](https://substack.com/redirect/ed0947ce-0ed4-4f7b-98be-318500f3aa85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))

Is the same thing happening with online gambling? Yes. We're seeing exactly the [same sort of impact happening](https://substack.com/redirect/12648571-533f-4722-be23-774b4167f4a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) now that people can gamble on sports without even leaving their couch:
> [The average credit score](https://substack.com/redirect/072256e6-6635-4d4d-b16f-fd815da58a44?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in states that legalized sports betting decreased by 0.3 percent -- and by one percent, three times the average, in states that allow online sports betting. These might seem like small shifts, but they represent averages for entire state populations. This implies that a relatively small group of intensive users -- "problem gamblers" -- are suffering major damage to their credit scores, dragging down the overall average... **Meanwhile, states that legalized sports betting saw significant[increases in bankruptcy](https://substack.com/redirect/f995963f-2473-4f57-b672-ef8715c6a96a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) filing rates and debt collections.** Debt consolidation loans went up 8 percent by dollar value, and auto loan delinquencies increased 9 percent.
As this article hints at, the damage that mobile sports gambling is doing is not evenly distributed:
* There's variable data on this, but men are between [2×](https://substack.com/redirect/0a46bef9-87e1-4df5-a0f9-b7822ada42ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [7.5× more likely than women](https://substack.com/redirect/550a4f0b-0f9c-4630-bb6f-f9a07f91d0a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to have a gambling problem. I couldn't find good data for this in the U.S., but in the United Kingdom, [94% of gambling revenue comes from men](https://substack.com/redirect/2a543934-1506-4dbf-b5f0-f523e4da08c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* Youths and college students--many of whom, it should be noted, are not 21 but are finding ways to gamble anyway--[are more likely to gamble and much more likely to develop a gambling problem](https://substack.com/redirect/27a333e4-d6bc-481b-9e4d-8cd70f1941f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* [Black people are twice as likely as White people](https://substack.com/redirect/c2a58c5b-a3da-4c89-87f6-644c4aa780f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to be gambling addicts.

I've written about [how hard it is to be a young man today](https://substack.com/redirect/c6f8affb-7216-4563-8fae-d07990d23f40?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and how we need policies to help them. Young men are hit hardest by legalized mobile sports gambling. **Amendment 2 will hurt young men especially; it 's the exact opposite of what we need.**
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=147244890&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTQ3MjQ0ODkwLCJpYXQiOjE3MjcwOTU3NjQsImV4cCI6MTcyOTY4Nzc2NCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.ut3CNoQNoRJvqiPENpEmCNsYn-E5cMgfM9oMFT4lCvw)
### Gambling is a legalized narcotic. Just ask the American Psychiatry Association
Prevailing wisdom is that people will find a way to satisfy their vices--drinking or gambling or whatever else--regardless of any policy decisions. Empirically, that is untrue. We're seeing that in states across the country.
Gambling is, clinically, a legalized narcotic. The American Psychiatry Association has a list of "Substance-Related and Addictive Disorders" that includes a lot of the culprits you'd expect: alcohol, meth, opioids, and more. [Gambling is the ](https://substack.com/redirect/ece919d9-1f7e-4768-b8da-29dca1e2030c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[only](https://substack.com/redirect/ece919d9-1f7e-4768-b8da-29dca1e2030c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ addiction that isn't directly related to substance use](https://substack.com/redirect/ece919d9-1f7e-4768-b8da-29dca1e2030c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Why? "Gambling disorder is similar to substance-related disorders in clinical expression, brain origin, comorbidity, physiology, and treatment."
2.5 million Americans--[1% of the adults in this country](https://substack.com/redirect/5307d443-b955-4985-a98c-f04e5bb9afc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--are severe gambling addicts. As many as eight million more are considered problem gamblers lower in severity.
To the extent that you buy the "Yes" campaign's [claims on its website that the amendment will raise tens of millions](https://substack.com/redirect/37ab66e7-5c7d-481a-ab21-631c1edad057?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for education--and as I noted above, you should be skeptical--even if we do raise that kind of money, we'd be creating all sorts of other issues:
1. Raising revenue this way will disproportionately fall on the backs of men, of young people, and of Black people. It will also, invariably, fall on the backs of addicts, for whom having access to a casino in their pocket will make it that much harder to quit.
2. With demonstrated [increases in bankruptcy](https://substack.com/redirect/f995963f-2473-4f57-b672-ef8715c6a96a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [debt](https://substack.com/redirect/2730cd07-f659-4b0c-988f-47e093796ced?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), it seems impossible to believe that we won't have to start spending more on social services.
3. As I [wrote about last time](https://substack.com/redirect/80fd246b-ec57-465c-bf05-ae568216dcb1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Missouri's professional sports teams are asking for, and are likely to get, [$1 billion in taxpayer support to build and rebuild their stadiums](https://substack.com/redirect/48e0ab14-434b-4837-b657-cae5c253574a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). If the state were serious about increasing teacher pay, [as the "Yes" campaign claims](https://substack.com/redirect/18ff886a-2779-446e-849c-c03001d0d91f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), they could do it now.

### Gambling leads to higher levels of domestic violence and suicide
Beyond just the financial losses, and the impact you'd expect that to have on individuals and their families, there are profound and wide-reaching impacts of gambling and gambling addictions.
1. [Problem gambling leads to increased rates of domestic violence](https://substack.com/redirect/23ce90a4-5fd9-448b-a848-f3c8a9a009bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). [Study](https://substack.com/redirect/ebcadee7-6d8d-4dbc-82e9-9746cbdd3a8f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [after](https://substack.com/redirect/525832ce-89f9-49de-bf9a-9eb6d73c9b7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [study](https://substack.com/redirect/5ef73822-5574-434a-9bcf-40d0d2ff7fdd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) demonstrates this relationship;6 [according to one study](https://substack.com/redirect/1951f059-b5b5-4407-ad24-f72f34e0eada?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), **25.4% of problem gamblers reported having perpetrated severe domestic violence**. It's a problem well understood to such an extent that many of the resources for recovering gambling addicts include resources for [domestic](https://substack.com/redirect/68520d94-1df0-4371-9ca6-ea8302b56821?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [violence](https://substack.com/redirect/55422d41-7b3d-4c71-869c-e935e595e3b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [too](https://substack.com/redirect/49959e85-d530-4f81-9282-b1c7d0f2c7c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
2. [Problem gamblers are ](https://substack.com/redirect/5ad6bdea-f4ef-40e9-8f80-5ff63fd33960?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[far](https://substack.com/redirect/5ad6bdea-f4ef-40e9-8f80-5ff63fd33960?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ more likely to have suicidal tendencies](https://substack.com/redirect/5ad6bdea-f4ef-40e9-8f80-5ff63fd33960?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Specifically, problem gamblers are 5-10× more likely to attempt suicide than people in the general population, and between 48-70% of Gamblers Anonymous members have contemplated suicide. **[Of any addiction, gambling has the highest suicide rate](https://substack.com/redirect/5d72402d-1209-4844-8b19-04a96691ff07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[.](https://substack.com/redirect/5d72402d-1209-4844-8b19-04a96691ff07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)7

Is mobile sports gambling responsible for domestic violence and suicide? Of course not. Those are challenging, multifaceted issues with a million different causes.
But we have seen what's happening in other states: people are gambling more than they can afford, and [more people are developing gambling addictions](https://substack.com/redirect/d5e481ec-0bd7-416f-8a5b-37412d72302b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). And the morbid reality is that by passing Amendment 2, all things held equal, rates of domestic violence will go up, and rates of suicide will go up.
### Let's fund education with the casinos that we have
Traditional, in-person casinos in the state are doing plenty well, because it's great to be in the business of legalized narcotics. An obvious example: Philip Morris, the tobacco company, was [the single best-performing stock over an eight-decade period](https://substack.com/redirect/34ffe78e-a432-4db5-a4a4-a21c3dfa6a00?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) between 1925 and 2007. If you bought $1,0008 of Philip Morris shares in 1925, you'd be a billionaire today.
I bring this up to say: **casinos can afford to pay more in taxes**.
In 2023, Missouri generated [about $400 million in tax revenue from casinos](https://substack.com/redirect/d640049f-af71-4597-b185-a8d40fbdf46c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which pay a [tax rate of 21%](https://substack.com/redirect/f754734b-99ee-43f3-a870-879ec15d41bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). That is, for context, [not actually that high relative to other states](https://substack.com/redirect/d2be3d56-3fb8-429b-a6d8-dd0ba8a6df50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with legalized gambling. In Rhode Island, the rate is about 61%; in West Virginia, it's 53.5%; in Pennsylvania, it's 54%; in Kansas, it's 27%.9
[Read the website for the Yes on 2 campaign](https://substack.com/redirect/37ab66e7-5c7d-481a-ab21-631c1edad057?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). They're claiming that it's all about education funding. So if that's what they care about, I've got an easier way to do it: **tax the casinos more**. Every 1% increase in the tax rate on casinos would generate an additional $20 million or so in tax revenue--more than Amendment 2 even claims it's likely to generate.
No need to bother with Amendment 2, which is so obviously harmful. If you actually care about education funding, let's just tax the casinos 1% more instead.

So $1,000 back then wasn't nothing, but no matter how you slice it: You would have done _extremely_ well having owned Philip Morris (the moral implications of that notwithstanding).

| | Happy Monday! Welcome back to another edition of our weekly Kean for Congress newsletter update! There are only __**43 days**__ until Election Day, and voting has already begun 🤯. This past week, our opponent's campaign pumped another **_$520,000_** behind her negative ad spend against Tom. But we are pushing back with your help - whether financial or on the ground. __Will you please continue to step up and chip into our mission by volunteering some time to call voters or knock on doors?__ Her frantic spending is a clear sign that we have the momentum. Our opponent is throwing as many resources as she can into the fight to try and move the poll numbers to attract outside help from Nancy Pelosi-backed Super PACs. If we can outlast her on the ground this week and next, the national radical democrats will have no choice but to abandon her efforts and focus elsewhere. For most of this week, Tom was in Washington to Chair committee hearings and vote on legislation. Tom has made a clear promise to NJ-07: He will fund the government responsibly and keep America open, no matter what the Democrats say. Upon his return to the district, he participated in events across three counties yesterday - including stops at community events, participating in parades, and honoring our veterans. Our Field Team continued organizing volunteers and local campaigns on the ground for our Get Out The Vote (GOTV) efforts. They spent the week hosting phone banks and launching on the ground door-to-door canvassing. We put up some impressive numbers you can read about below. | | This past week, Tom made stops in _**Warren Township**_ to support our local and county candidates, and gathered with volunteers and supporters in _**Long Valley**_ at a rally with California Congressman **Darrell Issa**! There are only 43 days until Election Day, and voting has already begun 🤯. This past week, our opponent's campaign pumped another $520,000 behind her negative ad spend against Tom. But we are pushing back with your help - whether financial or on the ground. Will you please continue to step up and chip into our mission by volunteering some time to call voters or knock on doors? Her frantic spending is a clear sign that we have the momentum. Our opponent is throwing as many resources as she can into the fight to try and move the poll numbers to attract outside help from Nancy Pelosi-backed Super PACs. If we can outlast her on the ground this week and next, the national radical democrats will have no choice but to abandon her efforts and focus elsewhere. For most of this week, Tom was in Washington to Chair committee hearings and vote on legislation. Tom has made a clear promise to NJ-07: He will fund the government responsibly and keep America open, no matter what the Democrats say. Upon his return to the district, he participated in events across three counties yesterday - including stops at community events, participating in parades, and honoring our veterans. Our Field Team continued organizing volunteers and local campaigns on the ground for our Get Out The Vote (GOTV) efforts. They spent the week hosting phone banks and launching on the ground door-to-door canvassing. We put up some impressive numbers you can read about below.
